name: move_player
summary: Cheat: move a player anywhere at once, to a point (at), next to a thing (to_id) or next to another player (near_player); works for a player on another machine. Ask the user first. Moves at once; dry_run reports where they stand.

help.text: player names who moves (a name or reference id; default the player, see player). Give one destination: at [x, y, z], to_id (land beside that thing, on the side facing the player, at its base) or near_player (beside that player). safe_ground drops the point onto the safe ground the game's own teleport and respawn use: the highest surface at that x and z (terrain or a roof), 4 m above it, away from lava and landers. The reply gives the player's place before and after, with the room of each, and moved_by (topic moving). A dry run moves nothing and reads where the player stands, so it checks a move a player's own game made.

moving.summary: Who makes the move: moved_by server, client or seat_exit.
moving.text: A player on another machine owns their own movement, so the server cannot simply set where they are. server: this game's own player, or a body no connected player controls; set here and read back. seat_exit: a player in a seat, bed, cryo tube or capsule leaves it and stands at the point, as getting up does; this reaches every player. client: a player on another machine; their own StationGod moves them when the order arrives, and after is the point sent. That needs StationGod of the same version on their game; without it the call is refused client_cannot_move and nothing moves.

refusals.summary: Why a player is not moved.
refusals.text: player_not_found and ambiguous_player list the players to choose from. player_not_movable: the player is dead, or another player is dragging them. outside_world: the point is beyond the world's terrain (the low-orbit area above the planet is allowed). client_cannot_move: the player's game cannot be reached (topic moving). thing_not_found for a to_id that is gone; no_local_player when no player is named and there is not exactly one.

player.description: The player to move: a name or reference id; default the player (see player).

at.description: Destination point [x, y, z] in metres (see positions).

to_id.description: Destination: beside this thing, on the side facing the player, at its base.

near_player.description: Destination: beside this player (a name or reference id).

safe_ground.description: Default false. true drops the point onto the highest safe surface at its x and z, 4 m above it.

dry_run.description: Default false. true reports the move and where the player stands, and moves nothing.
